title: Courtesy Credit for Periodic Fees Standing on a Savings Account
content:
Where periodic fees stand on an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts and a courtesy credit is due against them, that credit is put back onto the account as one courtesy refund entry.

The entry is booked against the fee entry whose reference number is given, so that the fee it answers is identifiable, and it carries the same fee code as that entry. The account's posted balance rises by the credited amount straight away, and the customer sees a courtesy credit line dated today and a higher balance.

### Recording the credit

The credit is recorded with the tool `credit_savings_courtesy_refund_0ed102a0`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. One call posts one courtesy refund entry.

### Parameters

`savings_account_id` — the reference number of the savings or money market account receiving the courtesy credit, taken from the savings account lookup.

`customer_id` — the customer reference number of the account owner, taken from the customer profile lookup.

`source_item_id` — the reference number of the fee entry the courtesy credit is booked against, taken from the savings account activity lookup.

`statement_cycle` — the statement cycle the courtesy credit itself posts in, being the month in which that cycle closes. It is written as YYYY-MM, and an empty value is not accepted.

`refund_amount` — the courtesy credit being posted, in USD to 2 decimal places, always positive. A value carrying more than 2 decimal places is stored rounded half up to the cent, and the bank's own Eastern Time posting date is used.

### What the call returns

A confirmation sentence carrying the reference number of the courtesy credit just created, the credited amount in USD to two decimal places, the reference number of the fee entry it is booked against, and the account's new posted balance in USD to two decimal places. That sentence is what indicates the credit completed.
